claim: KIF2A is an ATP-dependent microtubule (MT) destabilizer.
source: Kinesin super family protein 2A (KIF2A), an ATP-dependent microtubule (MT) destabilizer, regulates cell migration, axon elongation, and pruning in the developing nervous system.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: KIF2A regulates cell migration, axon elongation, and pruning in the developing nervous system.
source: Kinesin super family protein 2A (KIF2A), an ATP-dependent microtubule (MT) destabilizer, regulates cell migration, axon elongation, and pruning in the developing nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: KIF2A mutations have been identified in patients with malformed cortical development.
source: KIF2A mutations have recently been identified in patients with malformed cortical development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Cavallin et al., 2017; Poirier et al., 2013).

claim: Postnatal KIF2A is continuously expressed in the hippocampus.
source: However, postnatal KIF2A is continuously expressed in the hippocampus, in which new neurons are generated throughout an individual's life in established neuronal circuits.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by expression data in Figure 1B.

claim: New neurons are generated throughout an individual's life in the hippocampus.
source: However, postnatal KIF2A is continuously expressed in the hippocampus, in which new neurons are generated throughout an individual's life in established neuronal circuits.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is established knowledge in neuroscience, supported by citations (Gonçalves et al., 2016; Eriksson et al., 1998; Kaplan and Hinds, 1977).

claim: Kif2a-cKO mice showed no significant defects in neuronal proliferation or migration.
source: Despite exhibiting no significant defects in neuronal proliferation or migration, Kif2a-cKO mice showed signs of an epileptic hippocampus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Kif2a-cKO mice showed signs of an epileptic hippocampus.
source: Despite exhibiting no significant defects in neuronal proliferation or migration, Kif2a-cKO mice showed signs of an epileptic hippocampus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by EEG recordings and histological analysis in Figure 2.

claim: Kif2a-cKO mice exhibited mossy fiber sprouting.
source: In addition to mossy fiber sprouting, the Kif2a-cKO dentate granule cells (DGCs) showed dendro-axonal conversion, leading to the growth of many aberrant overextended dendrites that eventually developed axonal properties.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Timm staining data in Figure 4.

claim: Kif2a-cKO dentate granule cells showed dendro-axonal conversion.
source: In addition to mossy fiber sprouting, the Kif2a-cKO dentate granule cells (DGCs) showed dendro-axonal conversion, leading to the growth of many aberrant overextended dendrites that eventually developed axonal properties.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining and live imaging data in Figure 6.

claim: Postnatal KIF2A is a key length regulator of DGC developing neurites.
source: These results suggested that postnatal KIF2A is a key length regulator of DGC developing neurites and is involved in the establishment of precise postnatal hippocampal wiring.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: KIF2A belongs to the kinesin-13 family.
source: KIF2A belongs to the kinesin-13 family (M-kinesin: internal motor domain family) (Aizawa et al., 1992; Noda et al., 1995; Miki et al., 2001), which destabilizes MTs in an ATP-dependent manner (Desai et al., 1999; Howard and Hyman, 2007; Moores and Milligan, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The kinesin-13 family destabilizes MTs in an ATP-dependent manner.
source: KIF2A belongs to the kinesin-13 family (M-kinesin: internal motor domain family) (Aizawa et al., 1992; Noda et al., 1995; Miki et al., 2001), which destabilizes MTs in an ATP-dependent manner (Desai et al., 1999; Howard and Hyman, 2007; Moores and Milligan, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: KIF2A controls neurite elongation by regulating MT dynamics at neuronal growth cones in early stages of developing murine nervous system.
source: In the early stages of the developing murine nervous system, KIF2A controls neurite elongation by regulating MT dynamics at neuronal growth cones and plays a crucial role in neuronal migration, axonal elongation and axon pruning in vivo (Homma et al., 2003; Noda et al., 2012; Ogawa and Hirokawa, 2015; Maor-Nof et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: KIF2A plays a crucial role in neuronal migration, axonal elongation and axon pruning in vivo.
source: In the early stages of the developing murine nervous system, KIF2A controls neurite elongation by regulating MT dynamics at neuronal growth cones and plays a crucial role in neuronal migration, axonal elongation and axon pruning in vivo (Homma et al., 2003; Noda et al., 2012; Ogawa and Hirokawa, 2015; Maor-Nof et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: KIF2A mutations in residues Ser317 and His321 have been identified in patients with malformed cortical development (MCD).
source: Recently, studies of KIF2A function in humans have primarily focused on cortical development because KIF2A mutations in residues Ser317 and His321 have been identified in patients with malformed cortical development (MCD) (Cavallin et al., 2017; Poirier et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Both KIF2A mutants (Ser317 and His321) are expected to lose MT destabilizing activity.
source: Both mutants are expected to lose MT destabilizing activity, due to a disruption in ATP binding or hydrolysis, thus resulting in a classic form of lissencephaly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference based on the nature of the mutations.

claim: KIF2A mutations result in a classic form of lissencephaly.
source: Both mutants are expected to lose MT destabilizing activity, due to a disruption in ATP binding or hydrolysis, thus resulting in a classic form of lissencephaly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to patient studies.

claim: The expression of postnatal KIF2A throughout the brain is gradually restricted to specific brain regions, including the hippocampus.
source: After reaching its peak in the early postnatal weeks, however, the expression of postnatal KIF2A throughout the brain is gradually restricted to specific brain regions, including the hippocampus (Lein et al., 2007), in which new neurons are generated throughout an individual's life in established neuronal circuits (Gonçalves et al., 2016; Eriksson et al., 1998; Kaplan and Hinds, 1977).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Conventional Kif2a knockout mice die within 1 day of birth.
source: This postnatal expression pattern suggests that KIF2A might be involved in adult neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and the establishment of refined neuronal circuits in these brain regions, but this role has not yet been confirmed because conventional knockout mice die within 1 day of birth (Homma et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Tamoxifen injections in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice began in postnatal week 3.
source: We began tamoxifen injections in postnatal week 3 (3w), when the cortical neurons or major cranial nuclei had nearly completed their migration.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed successful neuronal migration.
source: The 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed successful neuronal migration, but all mice died by postnatal week 6 and showed signs of hyperactivity, weight loss, and temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: All 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice died by postnatal week 6.
source: The 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed successful neuronal migration, but all mice died by postnatal week 6 and showed signs of hyperactivity, weight loss, and temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed signs of hyperactivity, weight loss, and temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).
source: The 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed successful neuronal migration, but all mice died by postnatal week 6 and showed signs of hyperactivity, weight loss, and temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: In the postnatal hippocampus, KIF2A expression was histologically restricted to the dentate mossy fibers (MFs).
source: In the postnatal hippocampus, KIF2A expression was histologically restricted to the dentate mossy fibers (MFs), and the loss of KIF2A-induced MF sprouting (MFS) and aberrant recurrent excitatory circuits.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The loss of KIF2A induced MF sprouting (MFS) and aberrant recurrent excitatory circuits.
source: In the postnatal hippocampus, KIF2A expression was histologically restricted to the dentate mossy fibers (MFs), and the loss of KIF2A-induced MF sprouting (MFS) and aberrant recurrent excitatory circuits.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: In 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice, dentate granule cells extended aberrant axons through both the inner and outer molecular layers.
source: In our 3w-Kif2a-cKO mouse model, unlike the typical TLE mouse model, the dentate granule cells (DGCs) extended aberrant axons through both the inner and outer molecular layers (IML and OML, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Primary cultured P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs did not regulate axonal or dendritic length.
source: Intriguingly, primary cultured P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs did not regulate axonal or dendritic length, and consequently, the characteristics of the overextended dendrites changed, resulting in axonal conversion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: The characteristics of overextended dendrites in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs changed, resulting in axonal conversion.
source: Intriguingly, primary cultured P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs did not regulate axonal or dendritic length, and consequently, the characteristics of the overextended dendrites changed, resulting in axonal conversion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: KIF2A expression peaked at P14 in the hippocampus.
source: The expression peaked at P14.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption and shown in the Western blot in Figure 1B.

claim: KIF2A expression was lost within 1 week after the start of tamoxifen injection.
source: The loss of KIF2A. KIF2A expression was lost within 1 week after the start of the tamoxifen injection.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1D caption and shown in the Western blot in Figure 1D.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice developed smaller bodies than WT mice.
source: The 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice developed smaller bodies than the WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1E caption and shown in the photograph in Figure 1E.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed weight loss after the loss of KIF2A.
source: The cKO mice showed weight loss after the loss of KIF2A (n = 20, results indicate ± SD, *p<0.01; Welch's t-test).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1F caption and shown in the graph in Figure 1F.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed hyperactivity at postnatal week 5.
source: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed hyperactivity at postnatal week 5 (n = 10, error bar indicates ± SD, *p<0.01; Welch's t-test).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1G caption and shown in the graph in Figure 1G.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed epileptic convulsions during a 30-min observation during postnatal week 5.
source: The 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed epileptic convulsions during a 30-min observation during postnatal week 5 (five mice each from five independent experiments, error bar indicates ± SEM, *p<0.01; Welch's t-test).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1H caption and shown in the graph in Figure 1H.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice began to die starting in postnatal week 5, and all mice died by the end of week 6.
source: These mice began to die starting in postnatal week 5, and all mice died by the end of week 6.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1I caption and shown in the survival curve in Figure 1I.

claim: In the hippocampus, 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed aberrant spikes in the EEG that coincided with twitching.
source: In the hippocampus, 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice showed aberrant spikes in the EEG (arrowheads in Figure 2A) that coincided with twitching in the resting or locomotive state (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: During epileptic seizure, paroxysmal EEG events were clearly detected in the hippocampus but not in the cortex of 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice.
source: Moreover, during the epileptic seizure (Figure 2—video 1), the paroxysmal EEG events were clearly detected in the hippocampus but not in the cortex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The loss of postnatal KIF2A resulted in an epileptic hippocampus in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice.
source: These results suggested that the loss of postnatal KIF2A resulted in an epileptic hippocampus in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on EEG data.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO DGCs are larger than WT cells.
source: cKO DGCs are larger than the WT cells. The results are shown as the mean ± SD (7 slices each, n = 259 for WT, n = 233 for cKO). *p<0.01 (Welch's t-test).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2H caption and shown in the graph in Figure 2H.

claim: Long paroxysmal depolarization shifts (PDSs) were detected in cKO hippocampal slices.
source: The WT slice (I) did not yield a response, and long paroxysmal depolarization shifts (PDSs) were detected in the cKO slice (J).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2J caption and shown in the electrophysiology trace in Figure 2J.

claim: 4w-Kif2a-cKO mice clearly showed hippocampal sclerosis at postnatal week 12.
source: The typical features of hippocampal sclerosis in 4w-Kif2a-cKO mice at postnatal week 12. The 4w-Kif2a-cKO mice clearly showed hippocampal atrophy (A), including CA1 loss (B), sprouting MFs in CA3 (C), and hypertrophic granule cells (D).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 caption and shown in the images.

claim: The GFAP-positive area of the cKO mice was substantially wider than that of WT mice.
source: The GFAP-positive area of the cKO mice was substantially wider than that of WT mice. The results are shown as the mean ± SD (n = 15, three independent experiments. *p<0.01 (Welch's t-test)).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G caption and shown in the graph.

claim: The numbers of CldU- and IdU-positive cells were not significantly different between WT and 3w-Kif2a-cKO slices.
source: Importantly, the numbers of CldU- and IdU-positive cells were not significantly different between WT and 3w-Kif2a-cKO slices (Figure 3B, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The difference in cellular distribution between WT and 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice was not significant.
source: Migration histograms show that CldU-positive cells migrated farther than IdU-positive cells, but the difference in the cellular distribution between the WT and 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice was not significant (Figure 3H, compared with 3G, see also Figure 3I, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 3G-I.

claim: KIF2A is highly expressed in the dentate hilus and stratum lucidum at P21.
source: Note that KIF2A is highly expressed in the dentate hilus (Hil) and stratum lucidum (SL) (A) where DGCs extend their axons, termed MFs.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4A caption and shown in the immunostaining image in Figure 4A.

claim: An abnormally high dark brown density of Timm reaction product was observed in the stratum oriens and the entire dentate ML in cKO mice.
source: An abnormally high dark brown density of the reaction product was observed in the SO (yellow arrowheads in F) and the entire dentate ML (a yellow bar in H) in the cKO mice compared to that in the WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4 caption and shown in the Timm staining images in Figure 4F and H.

claim: Timm grain intensities in OML and IML were significantly higher in cKO mice than in WT mice.
source: Intensities in OML and IML were significantly higher in the cKO mice than in the WT mice. The results are shown as the mean ± SEMs (5 slices each, n = 6). *p<0.01; Welch's t-test.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4I caption and shown in the graph in Figure 4I.

claim: In the pilocarpine-induced TLE mouse model, Timm reaction products are observed only in the IML.
source: Positive control for the pilocarpine-induced TLE mouse model. Note that Timm reaction products are observed only in the IML (a yellow bar).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4J caption and shown in the Timm staining image in Figure 4J.

claim: The OML and IML intensities were significantly higher in CBZ-injected cKO mice than in WT mice.
source: The OML and IML intensities were significantly higher in the CBZ-injected cKO mice than in the WT mice. The results are shown as the mean ± SEMs (5 slices each, n = 8). *p<0.01; Welch's t-test.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E caption and shown in the graph.

claim: 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice had more NFM-positive axons in the ML compared with WT.
source: Compared with WT (A), 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice had more NFM-positive axons in the ML (B).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 caption and shown in the images.

claim: There is aberrant synaptoporin staining in the cKO OML.
source: Note the lack of obvious synaptoporin staining in the WT OML (D) but the presence of aberrant synaptoporin staining in the cKO OML (E).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 caption and shown in the images.

claim: More than 10% of outer mature DGCs in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice extended an aberrant axon recurrently to the ML.
source: However, 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice (Figure 5C), which were more than 10% of outer mature DGCs, extended an aberrant axon recurrently to the ML (similarly to the cell with a white asterisk), and more than 5% of outer mature DGCs extended aberrant axons directly from the cell body (similarly to the cell with a red asterisk) (Figure 5C and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5C and F.

claim: More than 5% of outer mature DGCs in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice extended aberrant axons directly from the cell body.
source: However, 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice (Figure 5C), which were more than 10% of outer mature DGCs, extended an aberrant axon recurrently to the ML (similarly to the cell with a white asterisk), and more than 5% of outer mature DGCs extended aberrant axons directly from the cell body (similarly to the cell with a red asterisk) (Figure 5C and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5C and F.

claim: Almost 30% of inner immature DGCs in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice had some aberrant protrusions on the cell bodies.
source: In contrast, among inner immature DGCs, almost 30% of the cells had some aberrant protrusions on the cell bodies (orange arrowheads of the cell with orange asterisk in Figure 5C and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5C and G.

claim: There were more ectopic DGCs in the 3w-Kif2a-cKO inner ML than in the ML of WT mice.
source: Moreover, there were more ectopic DGCs in the 3w-Kif2a-cKO inner ML than in the ML of WT mice (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The spine density of dendrites of outer mature cells was higher in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice than in WT mice.
source: In addition, the spine density of the dendrites of outer mature cells was higher in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice (Figure 5E) than in WT mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5D-E and I.

claim: The number of thin spines was specifically higher in both the IML and OML of 3w-Kif2a-cKO dendrites than in those of WT dendrites.
source: Morphologically, the number of thin spines, not mushroom or stubby spines, was specifically higher in both the IML and OML of 3w-Kif2a-cKO dendrites than in those of WT dendrites (Figure 5I, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 5I.

claim: More than 80% of cultured cells were Prox1-positive.
source: More than 80% of cultured cells were Prox1-positive (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B), and almost all cells had lost KIF2A expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Almost all cultured DGCs had lost KIF2A expression.
source: More than 80% of cultured cells were Prox1-positive (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B), and almost all cells had lost KIF2A expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: At DIV1, both WT and P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs generated a short Tau1-dominant axon and a MAP2-dominant dendrite.
source: At DIV1, both WT and P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs generated a short Tau1-dominant axon (Figure 6B and F) and a MAP2-dominant dendrite (Figure 6C and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6B-C and F-G.

claim: At DIV3, P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs gradually generated more aberrant axons than dendrites.
source: At DIV3, however, P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs gradually generated more aberrant axons than they did dendrites.
evidence: This is stated in the results text and supported by images in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In WT DGCs at DIV3, ankyrin G was detected at the neck of one axonal neurite.
source: At that time, in WT DGCs, ankyrin G, the marker of the axon hillock, was detected at the neck of one axonal neurite (an arrow in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs at DIV3, ankyrin G was detected in more than one neurite.
source: In the P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs, however, ankyrin G was detected in more than one neurite (arrows in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H) and the population of DGCs with multiple axonal nurites was significantly larger in P3-Kif2-cKO DGCs than in WT DGCS (Figure 6—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H and J.

claim: At DIV5, WT DGCs developed a single long axon and several dendrites.
source: Eventually, at DIV5, the WT DGCs developed a single long axon (a white arrowhead in Figure 6I) and several dendrites (a white arrow in Figure 6K), whereas P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs developed long, defasciculated, NFM-positive axons (white arrowheads in Figure 6J) and generated some dendrites with multiple additional axons around their cell bodies (Figure 6L).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6I and K.

claim: At DIV5, P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs developed long, defasciculated, NFM-positive axons and generated some dendrites with multiple additional axons around their cell bodies.
source: Eventually, at DIV5, the WT DGCs developed a single long axon (a white arrowhead in Figure 6I) and several dendrites (a white arrow in Figure 6K), whereas P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs developed long, defasciculated, NFM-positive axons (white arrowheads in Figure 6J) and generated some dendrites with multiple additional axons around their cell bodies (Figure 6L).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6J and L.

claim: A statistical analysis demonstrated significant neogenesis of aberrant axons in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs.
source: A statistical analysis also demonstrated significant neogenesis of aberrant axons in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs (Figure 6M green bars, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6M.

claim: The phenotypes of aberrant axon growth in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs were rescued by KIF2A transfection.
source: These phenotypes were rescued by the KIF2A transfection (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The neogenesis of aberrant axons in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs could be the result of a cell autonomous process.
source: The observations suggested that the neogenesis of aberrant axons in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs could be the result of a cell autonomous process rather than an altered response to the external environment, such as alterations in chemo-attraction/repulsion.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the results section based on the cultured cell data.

claim: The overextended dendrites in P3-Kif2a-cKO DGCs had axonal (Tau1-positive) rather than dendritic characteristics (MAP2-positive).
source: After the recording, the DGCs were fixed and stained with anti-Tau1 and anti-MAP2 antibodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 2H and I), revealing that the overextended dendrites had axonal (Tau1-positive, arrows in Figure 6—figure supplement 2I), rather than dendritic characteristics (MAP2-positive, arrowheads in Figure 6—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is stated in the results text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2I.

claim: The loss of postnatal KIF2A might disrupt axon/dendrite determination and induce the development of multiple short axons in the hippocampus.
source: These results suggested that the loss of postnatal KIF2A might disrupt axon/dendrite determination and induce the development of multiple short axons in the hippocampus, thus resulting in complex networks in the dentate gyrus.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: KIF2A loss at postnatal week 3 induced weight loss, hyperactivity, and eventually death with an epileptic hippocampus.
source: KIF2A loss at the postnatal week 3 induced weight loss, hyperactivity, and eventually death with an epileptic hippocampus (Figures 1E–I and 2D–K).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Postnatal KIF2A was strongly expressed in dentate MF at P21.
source: In the hippocampus at P21, postnatal KIF2A was strongly expressed in dentate MF (Figure 4A), and its loss induced MFS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and dysfunctional excitatory circuits (Figure 2J), whereas cell proliferation and cell migration were seemingly unaffected (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 4A.

claim: The loss of KIF2A induced MFS and dysfunctional excitatory circuits.
source: In the hippocampus at P21, postnatal KIF2A was strongly expressed in dentate MF (Figure 4A), and its loss induced MFS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and dysfunctional excitatory circuits (Figure 2J), whereas cell proliferation and cell migration were seemingly unaffected (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Cell proliferation and cell migration were seemingly unaffected in 3w-Kif2a-cKO mice.
source: In the hippocampus at P21, postnatal KIF2A was strongly expressed in dentate MF (Figure 4A), and its loss induced MFS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and dysfunctional excitatory circuits (Figure 2J), whereas cell proliferation and cell migration were seemingly unaffected (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: In the 3w-Kif2a-cKO dentate gyrus, younger granule cells developed aberrant protrusions.
source: In the 3w-Kif2a-cKO dentate gyrus, younger granule cells developed aberrant protrusions, and older cells developed aberrant apical axons and thinner dendritic spines (Figure 5B–5I).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: In the 3w-Kif2a-cKO dentate gyrus, older cells developed aberrant apical axons and thinner dendritic spines.
source: In the 3w-Kif2a-cKO dentate gyrus, younger granule cells developed aberrant protrusions, and older cells developed aberrant apical axons and thinner dendritic spines (Figure 5B–5I).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Abnormal morphogenesis of axons and dendrites was observed in Kif2a-cKO cultured DGCs.
source: Abnormal morphogenesis of axons and dendrites was also observed in Kif2a-cKO cultured DGCs (Figure 6J).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: KIF2A plays crucial roles in the development of the precise wiring of neuronal circuits in the hippocampus by controlling the development and maintenance of the neural processes of DGCs.
source: The results suggested that KIF2A plays crucial roles in the development of the precise wiring of neuronal circuits in the hippocampus by controlling the development and maintenance of the neural processes of DGCs (summarized in Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion based on all experimental results.

claim: KIF2A is a key axonal collateral suppressor of prenatal hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
source: Previously, KIF2A has been shown to be a key axonal collateral suppressor of prenatal hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The loss of KIF2A resulted in the activation of MT polymerization at the growth cone and the overextension of neuronal processes.
source: The loss of KIF2A, a MT destabilizer, resulted in the activation of MT polymerization at the growth cone and the overextension of neuronal processes (Homma et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Cultured DGCs expressed KIF2A in the cell bodies and dendrites at DIV1.
source: In addition to KIF2A expression in axons, cultured DGCs expressed KIF2A in the cell bodies and dendrites at DIV1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The activation of MT polymerization by CRMP-2 is crucial for axon/dendrite determination and morphogenesis in hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
source: The activation of MT polymerization by collapsin response mediator protein (CRMP)−2 is known to be crucial for axon/dendrite determination and morphogenesis in hippocampal pyramidal neurons (Bretin et al., 2005; Quach et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2016).
